answer: One short growing season a year is what tundra allows, and weight accrues only from a living vine rooted in the plot a public atlas assigns to one identity. Each epoch, inspectors measure tendril growth and match the root scan against the atlas entry; a dead, artificial, or transplanted vine fails the registered curve and earns no weight. A vine roots in one plot only, so no two identities can share its growth or borrow its root scan. Planting one vine costs an honest agent $25 once; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 rooted vines on 1,000 plots, $25,000 and a full season before any growth counts.
